display.title: Marbin B'Simchah: Adding Joy in Adar and the Lesson of the Mirror
display.summary_short: In Adar we add to the joy we always have and share it with others; the Baal Shem Tov teaches that a happy face is reflected back by our friends and by Hashem.
display.summary_long: A talk from the Tzivos Hashem radio show for the start of Adar. Uncle Yossi explains that serving Hashem with joy is a standing order all year, but the Sages chose their words carefully: when Adar comes we are 'marbin b'simchah', adding to the joy we already have. For a soldier in Tzivos Hashem this means making others happy too, since we love our fellow as ourselves, and the best way is to help a friend do a mitzvah, for, as Dovid HaMelech wrote, the mitzvos gladden the heart. We must also be a living example. The Baal Shem Tov taught that we can learn from everything, even a mirror: show a happy face and your friend's face will light up in return. He adds that the same is true with Hashem: when we serve Him with a smiling face, He shines back to us with joy and blessing, bringing the greatest joy of all, leaving golus with Moshiach.
display.lesson: Add to your joy in Adar, share it by helping others do mitzvos, and show a happy face: it is reflected back by your friends and by Hashem.
